title: WVPU New Student Scholarships
degree_levels: Austrian National Qualifications Framework (NQF) Level VI

funding_type: Tuition fee reduction scholarship (partial), with financial-need requirement

programme_action: WVPU New Student Scholarships, bachelor degree levels: Distinction / Merit / Honors
description: WVPU New Student Scholarships are awarded by Webster Vienna Private University to newly admitted bachelor's and master's degree students who combine academic achievement with demonstrated financial need. Awards are tuition reductions of EUR 12,000 (Distinction), EUR 7,000 (Merit) or EUR 4,000 (Honors) per academic year for bachelor's students, set against full-time undergraduate tuition of EUR 24,068 for 2026-2027. Up to 20 new students may receive a scholarship award per year. The scholarship can be renewed for the full duration of the bachelor's programme, to a maximum of four years, provided the recipient stays enrolled full-time and maintains a minimum GPA of 3.0. Applicants must first secure admission to a full degree programme and then submit the scholarship application during the published application period.

programme_structure.award_types_detail: Bachelor's level: Distinction EUR 12,000 per academic year (minimum 3.5 GPA, minimum C1 English proficiency, significant financial need, excellent essay and recommendations, newly accepted undergraduate student starting in Fall or Spring semester); Merit EUR 7,000 per academic year (minimum 3.0 GPA, minimum B2 English proficiency, significant financial need, strong essay and recommendations); Honors EUR 4,000 per academic year (minimum 3.0 GPA, minimum B2 English proficiency, financial need, good essay and recommendations). Master's level: Distinction EUR 8,000, Merit EUR 5,000, Honors EUR 3,000 per academic year.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Enrolled full-time (24 U.S. credits or 48 ECTS per academic year for undergraduates) and a minimum GPA of 3.0 each semester; renewable for the full duration of the programme, maximum four years for undergraduate and two years for graduate students.
programme_structure.intake: Two scholarship application cycles per year, tied to semester intake: Fall Semester cycle opens 1 March (deadline 31 May at 13:00 CET) and Spring Semester cycle opens 1 October (deadline 30 November at 13:00 CET).

database_notes: SUBSTITUTION: The assigned target, the Austrian Development Cooperation (ADC) scholarship administered by OeAD (historically the 'Development Cooperation Scholarships', applied for via oead.adam.at), could not be recorded because it does not exist as an open programme that funds bachelor's degrees. The host oead.adam.at no longer resolves, the Austrian scholarship portal is now grants.at, and the OeAD states plainly on its own studyinaustria.at site: 'We - the OeAD - do not offer any scholarships for a whole degree programme (bachelor's, master's or PhD) here in Austria.' The OeAD A-to-Z programme list contains no ADC / Development Cooperation scholarship; the only ADC-linked higher-education funding that still exists is APPEAR (master's and PhD, project-bound) and Cooperation Development Research (research projects). The nearest modern successor for full-degree funding of nationals of non-European developing countries, the Erhard Busek Grant (EUR 1,300 per month plus a one-time travel allowance of up to EUR 1,200), is restricted to a two-year master's programme and its own official page states 'At present, no further call for applications for the Busek Scholarship is planned.' It therefore also fails the bachelor's-level rule.

SUBSTITUTION: In keeping with the same slot number and filename, the record above is for the WVPU New Student Scholarships of Webster Vienna Private University, an accredited private university in Vienna, Austria. This is an open, bachelor's-level, tuition-reduction scholarship with verified euro figures and published deadlines. Substitution reason and evidence are recorded here rather than silently changing the target.
No widely-used acronym exists for this award, so the short form is the university's own published name 'WVPU New Student Scholarships'. There is no distinct legacy title.
bachelor_requirement is false because a completed bachelor's degree is not a prerequisite: the award funds a bachelor's degree and admission is based on secondary-school qualifications.
final_year_bachelor_allowed is false because applicants must already hold an offer of admission before the scholarship window opens, so secondary-school pupils still awaiting a decision cannot apply.

equivalent_degree_allowed is true as a statement of the admissions principle, but the scholarship page itself does not publish country-specific secondary-school equivalences and this was not separately verified.
multiple_applications_allowed, interview_possible, results_timing and application_fee are null because the official page does not address them. They are not asserted either way.

Recommendations appear in the award level criteria ('excellent essay and recommendations') but are absent from the document upload list, so the recommendation checklist entry is marked as unconfirmed rather than required.
The EUR 1,000 admission and registration deposit for new non-EU/EEA students is an admission charge, not a scholarship application fee, and is therefore not recorded in application_fee.

All monetary figures are quoted for the 2026-2027 academic year, which the university states are subject to change. Tuition of EUR 24,068 per academic year and EUR 12,034 per semester is the published full-time undergraduate flat fee, excluding summer term courses.
The EUR 26.20 per semester Austrian National Student Union (OeH) fee and other administrative fees are not covered by the scholarship.

The award is not a government scholarship: it is funded and awarded by the private university itself, and no Austrian state funding is attached to it. The Austrian Leistungsstipendium (StudFG sections 57 to 61) is a separate national award for students already enrolled at Austrian institutions and is generally not open to third-country nationals on a student residence permit, so it was not used as the substitute.

Deadline dates are published by the university as recurring month and day values with a time (31 May at 13:00 CET and 30 November at 13:00 CET) but without an academic year, so deadline_date is null and deadline_precision is 'typical_window', per the schema accuracy rule. The current cycle running on the verification date opened on 1 October 2026 and closes on 30 November 2026 at 13:00 CET.
The logo asset was confirmed live on the provider's own domain (HTTP 200, image/png, 35,675 bytes) and is used as the site logo on the official homepage and financial aid page.
